Arthur Fery backed to 'take risks and enjoy' Carlos Alcaraz clash at Davis Cup
Great Britain reach Davis Cup semis with 2-1 win over Germany; It means Arthur Fery now faces a potential clash with Carlos Alcaraz; Alcaraz has been nursing some injuries but is expected to take part in the semi-finals on Saturday
Friday 27 November 2026 11:35, UK
Leon Smith has told Arthur Fery to have no regrets if he gets the chance to play Carlos Alcaraz in the Davis Cup semi-finals.
Great Britain's upset win over Germany in Bologna on Thursday set up a mouth-watering clash with Spain as Smith's side bid to reach the final for the first time since claiming the title in 2015.
Fery will be playing just his fourth match in the competition but is set to face the world No 1 and No 3 back-to-back after losing to Alexander Zverev on Thursday.

Alcaraz sat out Spain's quarter-final win over Austria having won the ATP Finals last weekend despite nursing knee and hamstring issues, but it would be a surprise if he did not play singles - and potentially doubles - on Saturday.
Spain captain David Ferrer was keeping his cards close to his chest, saying: "I will see on Saturday. I don't know yet. But it could be possible."
Mixing in such circles is another indication of Fery's meteoric rise this season, and he was clearly disappointed not to be able to threaten Zverev.
Smith said: "I think it's another chance for him to go out and see what it feels like, then figure out ways that he can actually hurt Carlos.
"The more matches he gets at this level, which is still very, very new for him - I think embrace it, don't be scared of it.
"People hate hearing this 'free hit' thing. It kind of is. Just go out, express yourself. Don't come off the court with any regrets. Try to play safe in any way? No. Go and play. Go and take some risks. Shot make. Enjoy it."
Fery has not taken a set off Zverev in three meetings but this will be his first chance to test himself against Alcaraz, who is on a 14-match winning streak.
Speaking of the prospect, he said: "It would definitely be a massive challenge again.
"I think it would be a different style of play. That might help me. Also having had one match on that court in front of a lot of people against a top, top player, it would probably be good to have a second match on there and that would help me having that experience."
The tie is a rematch of Britain's last semi-final in the competition in Madrid in 2019, where a thrilling deciding doubles ended with Jamie Murray and Neal Skupski losing out to Rafael Nadal and Feliciano Lopez.
Skupski is the only remaining member of that team, and he will be looking to turn the tables if it comes down to the doubles again having produced a notable win alongside Henry Patten against German duo Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz.
Another factor is the British team's desire to finish on a high for Smith, whose tenure of nearly 17 years as captain will end after this week.
Spain are the favourites to win their first title since 2019 and are the only team with two top-10 singles players in Alcaraz and Rafael Jodar.
British No 2 Cameron Norrie claimed an impressive win over Jan-Lennard Struff on Thursday but has lost both his meetings with Jodar comfortably.
